content: The temporal gaps and generalized nature of the existing literature highlight a critical dependency on localized, timely research. The historic impact of conflicts in the Middle East has been a primary driver of major shocks in energy markets, leading to significant oil supply losses and fueling inflationary pressures on a global scale [54] . Geopolitical instability frequently disrupts the supply chains of essential commodities, including crude oil, natural gas, fertilizers, and staple foods [52] . Despite a consensus among experts regarding the general mechanics connecting geopolitics and commodity valuation, there remains a noticeable gap in comprehensive coverage detailing the cumulative impact of these events throughout the 2023 to 2026 period.
